question.text: A monkey of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> climbs on a rope which can withstand the tension <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>T</mi></mfenced></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>350</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. If monkey initially climbs down with an acceleration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> and then climbs up with an acceleration of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Choose the correct option <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>

options.text: Rope will break while climbing upward
Rope will break while going downward

solution.text:
Let a1 be the acceleration of monkey while moving down.

F.B.D of monkey while moving downward

Using Newton's second law of motion,

mg-T=ma1

∴  500-T=50×4⇒T=300 N

Let a2 be the acceleration of monkey while moving up.

F.B.D of monkey while moving up

Using Newton's second law of motion

T-mg=ma2

⇒  T-500=50×5

⇒T=750 N

Breaking strength of rope =750-300=350 N

∴  Rope will break while monkey is moving upward.
